However, the evidence states that the normal vector $n$ is derived from the cross product of tangential vectors ($n = t_u × t_v$). In standard vector mathematics, the cross product of two unit vectors results in a unit vector with components in the range [-1, 1], not [0, 1]. The evidence does not state that the normal vector components are bounded in [0, 1]; in fact, normal vectors typically have negative components depending on orientation. Therefore, the claim is only partially supported because it incorrectly generalizes the [0, 1] bound to all material properties, including normals, which are not described as being in that range in the text.
